errors: Index conventions are unstable on the page: both u^{n−1} and u^{n+1} appear as the second term of the α-sequence, and both ξ_{n−1} = ξ0' and ξ_n = ξ0' are written. These are working corrections, not a substantive error. Consistency requires the cyclic group to have order 2(n−1) when n−1 points lie on a half-circle.
Several numerical labels in the top figures are repeated (two 2's, two 5's, two 6's). They are labels of distinct events or antipodal pairs, not errors.

ideas.what: Sweeping a pseudoline through an arrangement by elementary triangle flips; the closed circuit of stable positions around a sub-stable position (a vertex)
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flips / mutations of pseudoline arrangements; topological sweep; local structure of the flip graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for flips; Edelsbrunner–Guibas (1986/89) for topological sweep; Goodman–Pollack for sweeps and allowable sequences

ideas.what: Boundary cyclic word with antipodal half-period, e.g. 0 2' 3' 4' 0' 1 2 3 4 1', and its change when a line is added
ideas.modern_name: Circular sequences / allowable sequences; encoding by the line at infinity

ideas.what: Circ(I∖{i0}) ← ĩ0: an oriented lift of a pseudoline induces a circular order on the other lines
ideas.modern_name: Local sequences of a pseudoline arrangement

ideas.what: Encoding the 2(n−1) crossing points on a pseudoline as an orbit of a cyclic group of order 2(n−1), with the antipodal map as the middle power u^{n−1}
ideas.modern_name: Z/2(n−1)-torsor structure on the circular sequence (antipodal cyclic order)
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in the oriented-matroid rank-3 literature (Bokowski, Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler)

ideas.what: Dependence of the sweep circuit on (side ρ, orientation ω), organized via {±1}-torsors and contracted products, plus operations σ_i on frames of the double cover (developed on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid/torsor bookkeeping of flags in the arrangement; action of a dihedral-type group on frames
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard credit in this form
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to among his 1980s 'géométrie topologique modérée' reflections (Esquisse d'un programme); unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a torsor/groupoid formalism for the space of positions of a pseudoline relative to an arrangement. Its ingredients are: stable versus sub-stable positions, monodromy circuits around vertices, and dependence on rive and orientation as {±1}-torsors with a cyclic Z/2(n−1) structure. The aim appears to be a functorial (groupoid-level) description of arrangement spaces. Standard oriented-matroid literature treats this only combinatorially, through flip graphs and allowable sequences, not as a stratified groupoid with explicit torsor data.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A groupoid or stack-theoretic treatment of the realization and flip spaces of pseudoline arrangements could connect with work on the topology of these spaces (e.g. Mnëv universality, Gelfand–MacPherson). On this page, however, the content is still elementary bookkeeping.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is standard pseudoline-arrangement combinatorics: sweeps, flips, circular sequences, antipodal cyclic order. It was known or being developed independently by Goodman–Pollack and others. The only distinctive element is Grothendieck's torsor-style bookkeeping, which is a working sketch rather than a result.
transcription_corrections: Bottom left, under '1 2 3 4': 'ξ0 ξ1 ξ2 ξ3 = ξ_{n−1}' (correct). The disk labels read ξ_{n−2}, ξ_{n−1} = ξ0', ξ0, ξ1 on the left/right and ξ1', ξ2', ξ_{n−2}' below; the order is spatial, not linear.

Rectangle sketch: the top row reads approximately '5 4 3 2 1' (first label somewhat unclear) and the bottom row '5' 4' 3' 2' 1'' (antipodal labels), drawn as a strip model of the Möbius band / projective plane.

Bottom-middle disk: labels are 3 (top), 2 (upper right), 1 and 0' (left end), 0 and 1' (right end), 2', 3' (bottom). The sequence '3 4 2 0' 0 1 1' 1 1' 2' 4' 3'' is a list of figure labels, not a formula.
'u^{n−1}' at the bottom centre is a subscript note under the row 'ξ0 ξ1 — ξ_{n−2} ξ_{n−1} = ξ0'', identifying ξ_{n−1} = u^{n−1}ξ0.
Top right: '6*', '10*' and a separate '10' near the right endpoint, with arrows indicating displacement of the endpoints.
